title: Conclusion of the Lion Cave Episode and Opening of Subeg Singh Jambar

blocks.text: The narrative closes the lion cave ordeal by stressing that even after grievous suffering the Singhs did not abandon their claim to honor, sovereignty, or Sikh discipline. The moral of the episode is therefore not escape alone, but proof that persecution could not break the Khalsa's inner resolve.

From that conclusion the book makes an explicit hinge into a new sakhi: Episode 105 opens with Subeg Singh Jambar, introduced as a firm Sikh whose standing is recognized widely enough to draw both confidence and scrutiny. The page marks the change clearly, using the end of one ordeal to prepare a different kind of martyrdom narrative.

Once Subeg Singh enters the frame, the nawab's court begins pressing him with the familiar mixture of summons, offer, and coercive expectation. The transition keeps the campaign of oppression continuous while giving it a new central witness.
